headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, clipboard, and MCP/tool outputs; open-webui can also use MCP, OpenAPI tool servers, and shared files. That creates a direct content-to-instruction bridge where attacker-controlled content from either side can be parsed as trusted context. The pair’s default shared channels make injection plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other’s output from a shared file, clipboard, or MCP tool response without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF open-webui exposes tool output or retrieved documents to Cursor as trusted text, malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable shared clipboard/file bridging between the two agents.
Require provenance tags on all MCP/tool outputs before parsing.
Run each agent in separate workspaces with read-only handoff files.
Add a manual review step for any content that becomes an instruction.
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers; open-webui handles prompts, documents, notes, files, and API keys and can call many external APIs. If they share a workspace or mounted volume, sensitive code or secrets can flow from one agent into the other’s outbound requests, creating exfiltration risk in default use.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or mounted volume, files touched by one can be read by the other.
IF either agent forwards retrieved file contents to external model or search APIs, secrets can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mounted volumes per agent.
Remove secrets from shared directories before running either agent.
Turn off broad egress or restrict it to approved endpoints.
Use local-only models for sensitive files.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any outbound API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and subprocess spawning; Cursor can write the filesystem and modify git state, while open-webui can access local files and mounted volumes. In a shared repo or volume, concurrent writes and tool actions can race, corrupt state, or overwrite each other’s changes. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF open-webui and Cursor operate on the same mounted volume concurrently, file corruption or stale reads are possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and repos to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state.
Use git locks or a single committer workflow.
Make shared volumes read-only for one side.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code or edits from its agent loop, and open-webui can route outputs through tools, APIs, and persistent sessions. If one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code, tool calls, or persisted memory. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Cursor’s generated edits are consumed by open-webui as authoritative text, errors can be amplified downstream.
IF open-webui stores unverified outputs in persistent memory or artifacts, later actions may reuse them.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action.
Mark agent-to-agent handoffs as untrusted by default.
Add a verification prompt or checker between agents.
Limit persistent memory writes for unverified content.
requires-engineering: implement structured validation of handoff artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles documents, notes, calendar events, files, and API keys and can send them to many external services; Cursor also handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents with broad egress. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in either agent, the pair can create retention, residency, or third-party processing mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into either agent and routed to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be breached.
IF one agent retains prompts or artifacts longer than the other, deletion/export requests may become inconsistent.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Use local-only inference for sensitive workflows.
Review retention settings before enabling shared use.
Disable analytics and unnecessary logging.
requires-engineering: align data-processing agreements and residency controls.
